protocolMetadata.instructions:
This is the Seqera MCP Server that provides AI assistants with access to containerized workflow tools and the Seqera Platform ecosystem.

            🔬 **Seqera Platform Integration**
            • Complete workflow management: launch, monitor, and analyze Nextflow pipelines on Seqera
• Complete Platform API access: 74+ tools covering all Seqera Platform operations including workflows, organizations, compute environments, datasets
• You can pull the latest runs that happened on Seqera with this toolset
• To create a new pipeline on Seqera you need to make sure that you have the proper compute environments associated with it
• Compute environment configuration (AWS, Azure, GCP, HPC clusters)
• Dataset management and sharing. These are csvs that just show where the data is, not the data itself.
• Access control and team collaboration            

🧬 **Wave Container Service**
• Create containerized environments with conda packages, pip packages, or custom Docker images
• Generate container build requests with automatic dependency resolution
• Support for bioinformatics tools from conda-forge and bioconda channels
• Perfect for creating containers for scientific computing and workflow execution for Nextflow pipelines
• If you get errors associated with the environment in your workflow, you can use these tools to create a container with the proper environment
• Perfect for scientific computing and workflow execution

🧩 **nf-core Bioinformatics Modules**
• Search 1000+ pre-built, standardized Nextflow modules using natural language queries
• Get comprehensive execution information including input/output schemas, command templates, and configuration examples
• Modules cover common bioinformatics tasks: alignment, variant calling, quality control, assembly, annotation
• Each module wraps popular tools (FastQC, BWA, samtools, etc.) with standardized interfaces
• Containerized modules with automatic dependency management

tool.name: search_seqera_api
tool.description: WHEN TO USE: When you need to help users accomplish tasks in the Seqera ecosystem (workflows, containers, packages) but don't know which specific API to call. WHAT IT DOES: Takes a natural language description of the user's goal and returns ranked suggestions of the most relevant Seqera APIs with complete parameter details and usage examples. USE THIS FIRST before call_seqera_api. AGENT GUIDANCE: Pass the user's intent directly - don't pre-process or guess API names yourself.

limit.description: AGENT INSTRUCTION: Request 3-5 suggestions for most cases, up to 10 for complex or exploratory requests. More suggestions = more options but longer response.

query.description: AGENT INSTRUCTION: Pass the user's request as-is, using their exact words when possible. Examples: 'show my running workflows', 'create a Python environment', 'find bioinformatics tools', 'set up cloud computing', 'help me analyze genomic data', 'I need to run a pipeline'. The more natural and specific, the better the API suggestions will be.

WORKFLOW: 1) Use this tool to find relevant modules, 2) Use describe_nfcore_module to get execution details. 3) Run it with Nextflow if required by the user.

tool.name: describe_nfcore_module
tool.description: Get comprehensive metadata and a ready-to-run Nextflow command for a specific nf-core module. CRITICAL: This tool returns ONE complete, executable Nextflow command in the 'READY_TO_RUN_COMMAND.nextflow_command' field - AI assistants should provide this exact command to users, not create custom workflows. IMPORTANT: Before running the command, the module must be installed locally using 'nf-core modules install <module_name>'. The response includes: detailed description, input/output schemas, and a production-ready execution command with Docker and Wave integration. Use this tool after finding a module with search_nfcore_module to get the exact command needed to run the module with the user's data. AI assistants: Always use the provided command exactly as-is, only help customize file paths.

tool.name: nfcore_suggest_analysis
tool.description:
Suggest appropriate nf-core pipeline and reference genome for analysis. Given library strategy and/or organism, returns recommendations for:

PIPELINE MAPPINGS:
• RNA-Seq → nf-core/rnaseq
• WGS/WXS → nf-core/sarek
• ATAC-Seq → nf-core/atacseq
• ChIP-Seq → nf-core/chipseq
• Bisulfite-Seq → nf-core/methylseq
• Amplicon → nf-core/ampliseq
• miRNA-Seq → nf-core/smrnaseq
• Hi-C → nf-core/hic

GENOME MAPPINGS (AWS iGenomes):
• Homo sapiens → GRCh38
• Mus musculus → GRCm39
• Rattus norvegicus → Rnor_6.0
• Danio rerio → GRCz11
• Drosophila melanogaster → BDGP6
• Caenorhabditis elegans → WBcel235
• Saccharomyces cerevisiae → R64-1-1
• Arabidopsis thaliana → TAIR10

Returns pipeline URL (nf-co.re) and AWS iGenomes S3 path for the genome.

_published_faq.name: How do I add seqera-mcp-server to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add seqera-mcp-server to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.seqera.io/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is seqera-mcp-server MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, seqera-mcp-server scores 78/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and does not yet meet Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is seqera-mcp-server's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, seqera-mcp-server scores 57/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 7 of 7 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to seqera-mcp-server?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to seqera-mcp-server in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.

_published_faq.name: How can seqera-mcp-server improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: search_seqera_api is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 54/100. Declare readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint based on the tool’s actual behavior. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
